applicationInfo.name: Bedrock Spend Controls threat model
applicationInfo.description:
### What this system protects

The Bedrock bill, bounded per identity, tenant, or workload; correct usage attribution; enforcement within the documented bound (metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation)); authorized and audited administration. Prompt confidentiality is out of scope: the broker never sees inference traffic and payload delivery is disabled.

### Method

STRIDE per trust boundary. Last updated 2026-09-15. The prose review with the reasoning behind every status lives in `docs/threat-model.md`; this workspace is generated from `docs/threat-model.json` by `tools/threat_composer_export.py`.

### Status legend (carried in each threat's Comments)

- **Mitigated** — A control exists in code and is covered by tests.
- **Accepted** — Known residual risk, documented, not planned.
- **Open** — No control; listed so it is not forgotten.

### Headline accepted risks

- The sample cannot constrain the account's management plane (T-12, T-26, T-27): apply the SCP.
- Workload mode has no permission lease (T-19): an IAM failure there is the only unbounded-overspend path; it is alarmed.

architecture.description:
### Trust boundaries

The editable architecture diagram is `assets/architecture.drawio` (page *Runtime-only architecture*); the data-flow page of the same file draws these boundaries.

| # | Boundary | Crosses | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Application / end user -> broker | OIDC JWT in X-Quota-User-Token; SigV4 on the AWS_IAM Function URL | `gateway/app/auth.py`, `gateway/app/main.py:_authenticate`, `cdk/stacks/spend_controls_stack.py (Function URL, invoker_principal_arns)` |
| B2 | Broker -> STS / IAM | AssumeRole with RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity = sanitized claim; inline session policy | `gateway/app/broker.py`, `gateway/app/session_policy.py`, `cdk/stacks/spend_controls_stack.py (BedrockUserRole, permissions boundary)` |
| B3 | Vended session -> Bedrock | IAM authorization of bedrock:InvokeModel*/CountTokens on allowed_model_arns; invocation log is the metering truth | `cdk/stacks/spend_controls_stack.py (role policy, boundary, invocation logging)` |
| B4 | Invocation logs -> usage processor -> DynamoDB | CloudWatch Logs subscription; identity.arn and modelId; transactional ledger writes | `usage_processor/handler.py` |
| B5 | DynamoDB streams -> enforcement processors -> IAM policy versions | REVOCATION# sentinels, CONFIG#EMERGENCY_STOP; CreatePolicyVersion on pre-attached policies; PutRolePolicy on workload roles | `enforcement_dispatcher/handler.py`, `revocation_processor/handler.py`, `emergency_processor/handler.py`, `workload_enforcer/handler.py` |
| B6 | Admin UI / API -> admin mutations | Shared admin key or admin JWT claim; separate break-glass key; If-Match + Idempotency-Key | `gateway/app/main.py:_require_admin`, `gateway/app/main.py:_require_emergency_admin`, `gateway/app/quota.py (admin mutations)`, `admin-audit table` |
| B7 | Operator / account administrator -> out-of-band IAM, SCP, logging | Console/CLI with account privileges | `DenyDirectBedrockPolicy (helper)`, `DEPLOYMENT.md SCP guidance` |

dataflow.description:
### Data flows

Red arrows in the diagram are trust-boundary crossings; `B-n` matches the architecture table.

- **DF-1** (outside) — End user / application → Identity provider (Cognito or corporate OIDC): OIDC login. Carries identity JWT.
- **DF-2** (B1) — Application backend → Broker Function URL: HTTPS, SigV4 (AWS_IAM) + X-Quota-User-Token. Carries JWT in; vended credentials and quota headers out (assets: vended credentials, quota configuration and subject status).
- **DF-3** (B1) — Broker → Identity provider discovery / JWKS: HTTPS only. Carries public signing keys.
- **DF-4** (internal) — Broker → Users table: DynamoDB conditional writes. Carries limits, status, VEND# rate counters, logical leases, SESSION# maps (assets: quota configuration and subject status).
- **DF-5** (B2) — Broker → AWS STS: AssumeRole with RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity and inline session policy. Carries temporary credentials for BedrockUserRole (assets: vended credentials, enforcement IAM policies).
- **DF-6** (B3) — Application (vended session) → Amazon Bedrock Runtime: SigV4 with vended credentials: InvokeModel*, Converse*, CountTokens. Carries inference traffic (payload out of scope), attributed by SourceIdentity (assets: Bedrock spend, vended credentials).
- **DF-7** (B3/B4) — Amazon Bedrock → Model invocation log group: service-side logging, payload delivery disabled. Carries identity.arn, modelId, requestId, token and image counts (assets: metering source).
- **DF-8** (B4) — Model invocation log group → Usage processor: CloudWatch Logs subscription filter (at-least-once). Carries invocation records (assets: metering source, usage ledger).
- **DF-9** (B4) — Usage processor → Usage table, Users table, CloudWatch, SNS: TransactWriteItems (REQUEST# marker + subject + per-model rows + RATE#); status update + REVOCATION# sentinel; EMF metrics; notifications. Carries priced usage, block decisions, detection lag (assets: usage ledger, quota configuration and subject status).
- **DF-10** (B5) — Users table stream → Enforcement dispatcher, revocation processor, emergency processor: DynamoDB Streams; iam:CreatePolicyVersion on pre-attached policies. Carries REVOCATION# sentinels and CONFIG#EMERGENCY_STOP -> deny policy versions (assets: enforcement IAM policies).
- **DF-11** (B5) — Workload enforcer (5-minute schedule) → Workload IAM roles: Ledger read; iam:PutRolePolicy scoped to the configured role ARNs. Carries inline Bedrock deny for over-budget workloads (assets: enforcement IAM policies, usage ledger).
- **DF-12** (B5) — Auto-block sweeper (nightly 00:05 UTC) → Users table, Usage table: Consistent filtered scan; TransactWriteItems conditional on version/status/reason. Carries automatic blocks lifted to active + REVOCATION# sentinel (assets: quota configuration and subject status).
- **DF-13** (B6) — Administrator (browser) → Admin UI (S3 + CloudFront) -> Cognito PKCE -> Identity Pool -> Broker admin endpoints: OIDC authorization code + PKCE; SigV4 with Identity Pool credentials; admin JWT group claim. Carries quota changes, blocks, enforcement dial, live leases, audit reads (assets: quota configuration and subject status, administrative audit trail).
- **DF-14** (B6) — Administrator / CLI → Broker admin endpoints: SigV4 + X-Admin-Key (Secrets Manager); break-glass key per emergency action; If-Match + Idempotency-Key. Carries admin mutations (assets: quota configuration and subject status, administrative secrets, administrative audit trail).
- **DF-15** (internal) — Broker → Admin audit table: Same transaction as the mutation. Carries immutable audit events and idempotency records (assets: administrative audit trail).
- **DF-16** (internal) — Broker → CloudWatch alarms/metrics, SSM roster parameter, Secrets Manager: Read-only: DescribeAlarms, GetMetricData, GetParameter, GetSecretValue at cold start. Carries operations view, workload roster, admin keys (assets: administrative secrets, price catalog and workload roster).
- **DF-17** (B7) — Spend reconciliation Lambda (opt-in, daily) → AWS Cost Explorer, Usage table: ce:GetCostAndUsage (resource *), ledger read, RECONCILE# write. Carries aggregate and per-workload-tag Bedrock cost for the settled day (assets: account cost data, usage ledger).
- **DF-18** (B7) — Operator → CloudFormation / CDK: Deploy with account privileges. Carries IAM roles, boundary, deny policies, logging configuration, SSM price snapshot and roster (assets: enforcement IAM policies, metering source, price catalog and workload roster).
- **DF-19** (outside) — SNS topic → Operator alert endpoint: SNS subscription (alert_email). Carries warnings, blocks, component failures.

### Assets

- **Bedrock spend** (A-1) — The account's Bedrock bill, bounded per user identity, tenant, or workload. The primary asset: every other asset matters because it protects this one. Goals: economy.
- **vended credentials** (A-2) — Short-lived STS sessions for BedrockUserRole carrying RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity = the sanitized identity claim and a lease-deadline session policy. Goals: integrity, confidentiality.
- **usage ledger** (A-3) — Usage table: canonical daily rows, per-model rows, RATE# minute counters, REQUEST# idempotency markers, and stored RECONCILE# runs. Goals: integrity, availability.
- **quota configuration and subject status** (A-4) — Users table: limits, thresholds, model budgets, status and status_origin, logical leases, SESSION# maps, REVOCATION# sentinels, CONFIG# control rows. Goals: integrity, availability.
- **administrative secrets** (A-5) — Routine admin key and break-glass emergency key in Secrets Manager; the admin JWT claim/value configuration that gates the console. Goals: confidentiality.
- **enforcement IAM policies** (A-6) — Per-user SourceIdentity deny shards, emergency deny policy versions, workload inline denies, the permissions boundary, and BedrockUserRole itself. Goals: integrity, availability.
- **administrative audit trail** (A-7) — Admin audit table events and idempotency records; CONFIG#ENFORCEMENT_AUDIT# and EMERGENCY_AUDIT# rows. Goals: integrity.
- **metering source** (A-8) — Bedrock model invocation logging configuration, the managed log group, and the CloudWatch Logs subscription to the usage processor. Goals: integrity, availability.
- **price catalog and workload roster** (A-9) — The reviewed price catalog and per-model overrides (configuration.py), the SSM price snapshot, and the SSM workload roster the console reads. Goals: integrity, confidentiality.
- **account cost data** (A-10) — Aggregate Bedrock cost for the Region read from Cost Explorer by the opt-in reconciliation Lambda and stored as RECONCILE# rows. Goals: confidentiality.

### Out of scope

- Prompts and completions: the broker never sees inference traffic and the logging configuration disables payload delivery, so their confidentiality is not a property this sample can affect.

assumptions.content: The identity provider is trusted and the attribute configured as jwt_user_claim is stable and not editable by the end user (the default sub is safe). Group membership behind admin_jwt_claim is managed by the IdP administrators.

Account administrators (IAM, SCP, Bedrock logging configuration, DynamoDB console) are trusted. The sample cannot constrain the account's management plane; production applies the SCP or DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and relies on CloudTrail for administrator accountability.

Model invocation logging is the metering truth: identity.arn, modelId, requestId, and token counts are populated by the Bedrock service and cannot be forged by the caller. requestMetadata is caller-controlled and is never used for attribution.

Model invocation logging does not capture StartAsyncInvoke, InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, or anything on the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Operators who need strict accounting exclude models used through those APIs from allowed_model_arns and deny bedrock-mantle:* alongside bedrock:*.

End users reach Bedrock only through vended credentials; workload-mode applications call Bedrock with their own IAM role attributed by an application inference profile. No other principal in the account retains bedrock:InvokeModel* (production enforces this with an SCP).

Overspend is bounded, not zero. The design guarantee is metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation); real-time cut-off is not a goal, and the bound must be measured in the deploying account (see qualification/QUALIFICATION.md).

Production restricts invoker_principal_arns so that only the application backends can call the broker Function URL; the broker is never exposed to anonymous callers, and token theft alone is insufficient to vend.

The routine admin key and the break-glass key are held by operators, rotated per the gateway runbook, and never reach a browser: the console authorizes by admin JWT group and SigV4, and the break-glass key is typed per action.

The reviewed price catalog and its overrides change only through Git review; the SSM price snapshot and workload roster are written only by CloudFormation, so a wrong price is a review failure rather than a runtime attack.

Reconciliation is opt-in. When enabled it reads Cost Explorer for the settled day (reconcile_lag_days) and the cost-allocation tag has been activated at the payer account; Cost Explorer data is account-wide by nature.
This is educational sample code, not a managed service: an adopter runs their own security review and adapts invoker_principal_arns, allowed_model_arns, the SCP, and alerting before production use.

A SESSION# map row cannot be needed after the STS credential it describes has expired (at most 3 600 s), so a usage_retention_days TTL with a 31-day floor only loses attribution for records delivered days late.

mitigations.content: Signature verified against issuer JWKS (RS/ES) or dev-only HS256; iss/aud/exp enforced; discovery and JWKS must be HTTPS; lease deadline capped at token exp so a replayed token cannot mint credentials that outlive it.
Reserved prefixes and the workload: namespace are rejected; documentation directs operators to a stable IdP-controlled claim (default sub).

Per-identity vend rate limit (VEND#<user>#<minute>, vend_rate_limit_per_minute) -> 429, summed across processes; one logical lease per identity: a new lease ID before refresh_after joins the current lease without extending its deadline; Function URL requires a SigV4 principal from invoker_principal_arns.
Headers describe only the authenticated identity's own limits.

session_name_for derives a collision-resistant name (sanitized prefix + hash of the full claim) and the same value is SourceIdentity; the exact stamped value is persisted on the user row (source_identity) so revocation never re-derives it; SESSION# reverse map; SetSourceIdentity/TagSession granted only to the broker role on the trust policy.

Never read for attribution; only identity.arn (Bedrock-populated) and modelId are used.

metadata.value: Code: cdk/stacks/spend_controls_stack.py; reconciliation_processor/handler.py | Tests: tests/test_cdk_stack.py; tests/test_reconciliation_processor.py

mitigations.content: Managed log group and logging configuration are RemovalPolicy.RETAIN; writer role trust is condition-scoped to aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn. Opt-in reconciliation (reconciliation_enabled) is the detection control.

Overspend bounded by construction: metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation); lease deadline embedded in the credential and non-extending on retry; DetectionLagMilliseconds measured per record.
One TransactWriteItems with a conditional REQUEST#<id> marker Put plus subject and per-model ledger Updates; a cancelled transaction re-reads the marker before classifying as duplicate.
Logged as unresolved_sessions warning; retention floor 31 days; a session cannot outlive the vended STS credential (<= 3600 s).
Propagation is inside the documented bound; the lease is the fallback.

Processor keeps the last-good deny set rather than clearing it; RevocationPolicyOverflowAlarm; lease still bounds new identities; shard count immutable to prevent rehash gaps. The nightly auto-block sweep (T-31) evicts identities whose automatic block is already stale, so shard capacity is consumed only by currently over-quota subjects.

Revocation and emergency processors may only version their designated pre-attached policy ARNs (no AttachRolePolicy/CreatePolicy/role edits); the vended role's permissions boundary caps any policy version; workload enforcer PutRolePolicy scoped to exact configured role ARNs; emergency processor DynamoDB access restricted with dynamodb:LeadingKeys.
WorkloadEnforcementFailureAlarm; 5-minute repair schedule; manual attach procedure in the runbook.
Dispatcher fan-out design; synth test asserts exactly two EventSourceMappings.

Criterion is the broker's own (row_enforcement.over_budget in the shared layer, also exercised by the workload-enforcer suite); only automatic-origin rows are candidates and status_origin admin is never written; each lift is a TransactWriteItems conditional on observed version/status/status_reason so a concurrent admin block or re-block wins and the sweep counts a race; the REVOCATION# sentinel rides in the same transaction so row and deny shards cannot disagree; no iam:* permissions; a wrongly lifted subject is re-blocked at its next vend or metered request through the existing paths.

Both keys in Secrets Manager, read at cold start, never sent to the browser (UI authorizes by admin JWT claim); break-glass key entered per action and not persisted; empty ADMIN_JWT_CLAIM disables JWT admin; both compares constant-time via secrets.compare_digest.
Claim/value are operator-configured; IdP group membership is outside the sample.

Every create/limit/status/model-budget mutation writes an immutable audit event (actor, auth method, reason, before/after) and a request-hash-bound idempotency marker in the same transaction; If-Match versioning rejects lost updates; enforcement-dial and emergency actions write their own immutable audit rows.
UI requires explicit confirmation and a reason for Unlimited, period changes, and alert-only thresholds; all changes audited.
Operations exposes alarm keys/states, metric values, and configuration numbers only; never secret ARNs, policy ARNs, or the emergency key.

metadata.value: T-01 — status Accepted. Boundary B1: Application / end user -> broker. Residual: A token stolen before exp is usable until then; no jti replay cache. Caller must also hold a SigV4 principal allowed on the Function URL.

threats.prerequisites: who has captured a valid user JWT before its expiry and also holds an IAM principal allowed on the broker Function URL
threats.threatAction: present the captured token to the broker
threats.threatImpact: credentials vended under the victim's identity and spend charged to the victim's quota until the token expires
threats.statement: An external actor who has captured a valid user JWT before its expiry and also holds an IAM principal allowed on the broker Function URL can present the captured token to the broker, which leads to credentials vended under the victim's identity and spend charged to the victim's quota until the token expires, resulting in reduced integrity and economy of vended credentials, Bedrock spend and usage ledger

metadata.value: T-02 — status Accepted. Boundary B1: Application / end user -> broker. Residual: IdP configuration is outside the sample.

threats.threatAction: set their quota identity claim to another subject's value
threats.threatImpact: spend accounted to and blocks applied against the wrong subject
threats.statement: An authenticated user whose IdP lets them edit the attribute configured as jwt_user_claim (for example a self-service preferred_username) can set their quota identity claim to another subject's value, which leads to spend accounted to and blocks applied against the wrong subject, resulting in reduced integrity and economy of usage ledger, quota configuration and subject status and Bedrock spend

metadata.value: T-03 — status Mitigated. Boundary B1: Application / end user -> broker. Residual: Many valid identities multiply the per-identity budget; SigV4 scopes who can try.

threats.threatAction: request credentials in a tight loop
threats.threatImpact: STS AssumeRole throttling and DynamoDB write pressure that starve other users' vends
threats.statement: An authenticated client with a valid JWT and an allowed SigV4 principal can request credentials in a tight loop, which leads to STS AssumeRole throttling and DynamoDB write pressure that starve other users' vends, resulting in reduced availability of vended credentials

threats.statement: An authenticated user holding a vend response can read another subject's limits or usage from the quota response headers, which leads to disclosure of a third party's budget and consumption, resulting in reduced confidentiality of quota configuration and subject status and usage ledger
